invariant_notes.H3_no_double_delivery: EARNED 2026-08-24 (P05). Established by four independent mechanisms, because no single one suffices: (1) real process concurrency via multiprocessing/spawn, one parametrisation oversubscribed (48 requested from a pool of 24) -> 24 unique, 0 duplicates; (2) a COMMITTED negative control, NaiveStore's read-then-write lease, which the same assertion catches at 30 duplicates on an IDENTICAL config (pool 12, 6 procs x 6) where the real store gives 0 -- without this the green result would be indistinguishable from a test that never created contention; (3) an independent append-only lease_log audit, double_delivery_violations(), which examines what happened instead of asking lease() to report on itself; (4) AST guards on structure, since the correct and broken implementations are behaviourally identical single-threaded. Artifact: engineering/raw/lease_concurrency.json.
invariant_notes.H7_live_not_good: EARNED 2026-08-24 (P04). The gate exists, is pure, and refuses on zero evidence (NOT_MEASURED). Replayed against the legacy system's OWN 102 admitted proxies it rejects 97 (95.1%), all on TOO_SLOW_P95. CAVEAT recorded honestly: that replay is k=1 because the legacy file holds one sample per proxy, so it tests the THRESHOLD only -- k=5 sampling, jitter and reliability are exercised by unit tests, not yet by live measurement. Live calibration is P06.
invariant_notes.H8_crash_resume: EARNED 2026-08-24 (P05). SQLite WAL + synchronous=FULL. A child process writes, prints an ACK, then os.kill(os.getpid(), SIGKILL); the parent asserts returncode == -9 (signal 9 is uncatchable, so no finally/atexit/context manager ran) and then reopens the db and finds every acknowledged row. Exports are .tmp + fsync + os.replace in the SAME directory, with the fsync-before-replace ORDER asserted by AST -- a reader never observes a truncated file.
invariant_notes.H1_evidence_for_every_claim: Re-earned 2026-08-24. Two ADRs were documented without implementation and the README cited unmeasured numbers; caught, recorded in RECONCILIATION.md 5-6, and now enforced by gate_check.adr_claims_are_verifiable (ADR-014).
